oil.summary: Crude markets settled in a split session today. WTI firmed 1.09% to $96.12/bbl, supported by a bullish EIA print showing US inventories down 8.6 million barrels for the week ending Oct 9. Brent slipped modestly to $105.62, pressured by the IEA's announcement of an accelerated emergency release of over 20 million barrels of diesel. The distillates complex bore the brunt of selling: RBOB collapsed 7.12% and Heating Oil shed 6.63%, though analysts warn the diesel crunch will persist well into 2027. Geopolitical noise remains intense—Iranian drone attacks (24 reported) are slowing Hormuz tanker traffic, Ukraine struck Russia's Ryazan refinery with drones, and the short-lived Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire appears to have already collapsed. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Massive US crude inventory draw of 8.6 million barrels provided a floor for WTI
IEA emergency diesel release and historic distillate selloff—RBOB -7.1%, Heating Oil -6.6%—dominate the product curve
Geopolitical escalation on multiple fronts: Iranian drone attacks on Hormuz shipping, Ukraine strike on Ryazan refinery, and Russia-Ukraine ceasefire breakdown

gas.summary: Natural gas prices held a constructive tone on both sides of the Atlantic, though from very different levels. Henry Hub edged up 0.53% to $3.215/MMBtu, extending a strong month that has seen prices rise over 11%. TTF dipped 0.73% to €86.5/MWh but remains near its highest levels since late 2022, up nearly 10% on the week. The common thread is Hormuz disruption: Qatari and UAE LNG flows through the strait remain severely curtailed, tightening European supply and leaving Pakistan at risk of winter shortfalls. News flow on gas-specific fundamentals is thin beyond the Hormuz LNG choke story; a headline on Exxon's Guyana operations suggests associated gas there may be retained domestically rather than exported.
drivers: LNG flows from Qatar and UAE through the Strait of Hormuz remain severely disrupted, driving TTF close to 2022 highs
Henry Hub up 11% month-on-month, reflecting tighter global LNG balance with Hormuz constraints diverting supply
Pakistan flagged as a near-term demand flashpoint facing winter shortages if Hormuz LNG routes stay choked

power.summary: Power and carbon news flow today was geopolitically heavy but light on direct power-price catalysts. EU EUAs slipped 1.13% to $82.71/EUA, pulling back modestly after a 1.53% weekly gain; the month remains mildly positive at +1.93%. TTF's sustained elevation at €86.5/MWh—up ~11% on the month—continues to underpin carbon as gas-fired generation becomes more expensive and utilities seek permit cover. Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles at Ukraine's power grid earlier this week, a direct infrastructure threat. On the supply-security side, the sole US commercial uranium enrichment facility (Urenco) reached 75% completion on its expansion, inching the country toward nuclear fuel independence. US Secretary of State Rubio's engagement with Central Asian republics on energy and critical minerals signals longer-term strategic diversification efforts.
drivers: Elevated TTF (€86.5/MWh, +10.85% monthly) keeps upward pressure on EU carbon as gas generation costs rise
Russia's 39-missile strike on Ukraine's power grid highlights critical infrastructure vulnerability across the region
Urenco US enrichment expansion at 75% completion marks a structural step toward domestic nuclear fuel security
